name: Webwall QR Campaign Tracker
author: webwall

sections.description:
Webwall QR Campaign Tracker is a QR code tracking and analytics plugin for WordPress designed to help businesses, agencies, and marketing teams measure the performance of offline campaigns.

Create trackable QR codes, use WordPress-powered short links, monitor QR code scans, and analyze campaign performance from a central dashboard.

Whether you use QR codes on flyers, brochures, posters, packaging, business cards, events, retail displays, or other printed materials, Webwall QR Campaign Tracker helps connect offline marketing activity with measurable digital results.

QR Code Tracking for WordPress

Create QR codes with tracked short links and measure what happens when people scan them.

Each QR code uses a WordPress redirect URL such as:

/r/{short_code}

When the QR code is scanned, the plugin records the scan and redirects the visitor to the destination URL.

This allows you to measure QR campaign activity without relying on an external QR tracking service.

QR Analytics & Scan Tracking

Monitor QR code performance directly from WordPress.

The dashboard provides QR scan analytics and campaign insights that help you understand how your QR codes are being used.

Track and analyze:

  • QR code scans
  • Scan activity over time
  • Campaign performance
  • Device information
  • Referrer information when available
  • Top-performing QR codes
  • Client and project activity

QR Campaign Management

Organize QR codes around real marketing activity.

Webwall QR Campaign Tracker supports:

  • Clients
  • Projects
  • Subprojects
  • Multiple QR codes
  • Campaign organization
  • QR performance reporting

This makes the plugin particularly useful for marketing agencies and businesses managing multiple offline campaigns.

Offline Marketing Campaign Tracking

QR codes can turn physical marketing materials into measurable campaign touchpoints.

Use Webwall QR Campaign Tracker for QR tracking on:

  • Flyers
  • Brochures
  • Posters
  • Product packaging
  • Business cards
  • Store displays
  • Events
  • Printed advertisements
  • Promotional materials
  • Direct mail campaigns

Instead of simply sending visitors to a URL, you can measure the scans generated by each QR code and compare campaign activity.

Privacy-Focused QR Analytics

The free plugin does not require an external analytics or QR tracking service at runtime.

QR tracking data remains under your WordPress installation.

IP addresses are not stored directly. Where applicable, the plugin stores a one-way IP hash for analytics and scan deduplication purposes.

Privacy and retention controls are available from the plugin settings.

Key Features

  • Create trackable QR codes
  • QR code scan tracking
  • QR analytics dashboard
  • WordPress-powered tracked redirects
  • Campaign performance metrics
  • Client organization
  • Project and subproject organization
  • Scan trends and charts
  • Device insights
  • QR code downloads
  • Safe URL validation
  • Redirect hardening
  • Privacy and retention controls
  • Local runtime assets
  • No required third-party tracking service

Built for Businesses and Marketing Agencies

Webwall QR Campaign Tracker can be used by individual businesses as well as agencies managing QR campaigns for multiple clients.

Create separate clients and projects, organize campaign QR codes, and review scan activity from one WordPress dashboard.

Why Track QR Codes?

A standard QR code tells you where visitors should go.

A tracked QR code can also help you understand whether your offline campaign is generating engagement.

Webwall QR Campaign Tracker provides the connection between printed marketing materials and measurable WordPress analytics.

Create the QR code, place it in your campaign, and monitor the resulting scan activity directly from WordPress.
sections.installation:
1. Install Webwall QR Campaign Tracker from the WordPress Plugin Directory or upload the plugin ZIP.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Open Webwall QR Tracker in your WordPress admin dashboard.
  4. Create a client or project.
  5. Create your first trackable QR code.
  6. Add the QR code to your printed or offline marketing material.
  7. Monitor QR scans and campaign performance from the dashboard.
sections.faq:
Can I track QR code scans in WordPress?

Yes. Webwall QR Campaign Tracker creates tracked QR redirects and records scan activity so you can monitor QR code performance directly from WordPress.

Does the plugin create QR codes?

Yes. You can create QR codes connected to tracked WordPress short links and download them for use in offline marketing materials.

Can I use it for marketing campaign tracking?

Yes. The plugin is designed for QR-based offline campaign tracking. You can organize QR codes by clients, projects, and subprojects and monitor scan activity for different campaigns.

Can agencies manage QR campaigns for multiple clients?

Yes. Client and project organization is built into the plugin, making it suitable for agencies managing multiple QR campaigns.

What types of campaigns can I track?

You can use tracked QR codes on flyers, brochures, posters, packaging, business cards, retail displays, events, advertisements, direct mail, and other physical marketing materials.

Does QR tracking require an external service?

No third-party QR tracking or analytics service is required by the free plugin at runtime. Tracking and analytics are handled through your WordPress installation.

What data is stored for QR scans?

Scan records may include a one-way IP hash, user agent, referrer URL, device type, bot flag, and timestamp. Raw IP addresses are not stored.

Can I delete tracking data?

Yes. Privacy and retention controls are available. By default plugin data is preserved on uninstall, but delete-on-uninstall can be enabled in the plugin settings.

Does the plugin load external CDNs?

No. Runtime assets, including chart assets, are bundled locally.

  • Improved client-to-QR relationship counting logic.

  • Added Upgrade to Pro dashboard UI.
  • Added Compare Plans interface.
  • Added Freemius upgrade integration.
  • Improved admin dashboard UX and premium upsell flow.
  • Hardened WordPress.org free package compatibility.
  • General cleanup and release stabilization.

1.5.5

  • Removed premium/pro code paths from the WordPress.org free package to keep only fully functional free features.
  • Removed Freemius references from the free package and improved WordPress.org compliance hardening.

1.5.4

  • Hardened upload path resolution and deletion safeguards for QR assets.
  • Hardened client IP extraction defaults for analytics and scan logging quality.
  • Restricted diagnostics/log output behind explicit WEBWALL_QR_DEBUG admin-only guard.
  • Fixed bot-exclusion setting persistence in admin settings.

1.5.3

  • Removed temporary development upgrade notice content from packaged readme output.
  • Improved release packaging consistency for WordPress.org free distribution.

1.5.2

  • Removed temporary update debugging endpoint and related troubleshooting helpers.

1.5.1

  • Added update targeting stability improvements.
  • Updated plugin/runtime version references for release verification.

1.4.0

  • Added legacy token migration utility and shortcode collision retries.
  • Added redirect safety hardening and expanded scan anti-abuse controls.
  • Added QA checklist documentation.

1.3.0

  • Implemented GDPR export/erase callbacks for scan metadata handling.

1.2.3

  • Added uninstall safety controls and retention settings.
  • Improved analytics uniqueness calculation and security checks.
